messages:
ana: Heads up — we had a subtle double-reserve case in staging when clients retried a request during a quota-check timeout. Not fully sure of the root cause yet, but saw 2 reserve ledger entries for the same Idempotency-Key.

mike: ugh. can you paste the trace + the request headers? did the client retry with the same Idempotency-Key or a new one?

ana: client sent the same Idempotency-Key. Logs show: 
```
POST /v1/generate 200
Idempotency-Key: pfx-12345
X-Org-ID: org_99
quota-check: timeout after 1500ms
reserve: created reserve_id=r_abc123
commit: client retried, reserve created again r_def456
```
Notably the reserve endpoint returned 202 async and our handler allowed creating a second reserve before the first resolved.

sasha: hmm, so the dedupe is happening at the top-level request path, but reserves are a separate flow that don't honor the same idemp key. If the first reserve hadn't written the final ledger record yet, second reserve wins.

lee: sounds like our current protection is per-request idemp at the API gateway which dedupes identical bodies for 10s, but the reserve path is internal and uses optimistic inserts without a uniqueness constraint.

billing-bot: Automatic note: possible duplicate ledger entries detected for org_99 between 2024-11-01T03:12:46Z and 2024-11-01T03:12:47Z.

ana: concrete problem: retries (network timeout) -> gateway retries same idemp -> our quota check path times out once, customer retries -> two different reserve_ids are created and later both committed -> double charge. We need a robust approach.

mike: options: 1) enforce a global idempotency table keyed by (org, Idempotency-Key) that any reserve/commit flow checks atomically before creating new ledger rows. 2) return a single canonical reserve_id for a given idemp key (cache + lock). 3) change flow to one-phase commit: reserve is implicit in create and commit is just finalise, but must be atomic.

sasha: +1 on global idemp table. Implementation idea: a small ACID row in Postgres with unique(org, idemp_key) and state {pending, committed, rolled_back}. Reserve creation does INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING then returns existing row if conflict. This prevents two reserves.

lee: that solves the create race, but we also need to handle TTLs and blockers: some clients send idemp keys per-request and never call commit (leaks). So we need an expiry and a reconcile job to roll back abandoned pending records and release quota.

mike: agree. Also telemetry: we should surface metrics when a reserve hits ON CONFLICT and we return the existing reserve_id so we can see how often retries happened. Add traces so we can connect original request trace_id -> reserve_id.

ana: we also need to think about per-key vs per-org rate limiting: if we dedupe on idemp at the organ level, that still works for multi-key clients. But per-key quotas could be bypassed: client rotates keys to bypass per-key bursts. We should keep per-org burst controls for cost protection and per-key for fairshare.

sasha: UX constraint: console rollouts for this will show noisy alerts if we change semantics. We should be backwards compatible: for older clients, we allow existing flow but mark them for migration. For new behavior, return explicit header `X-Reserve-Id: r_xyz` and `Idempotency-Status: reused|created` so SDKs can observe reuse.

lee: quick example API change suggestion: 
```
POST /v1/reserve
Headers: Idempotency-Key: <idemp>
200 { "reserve_id": "r_xyz", "status": "created" }
200 (conflict) { "reserve_id": "r_xyz", "status": "reused" }
```
This makes intents explicit and lets the client avoid retrying on reuse.

mike: implement plan: 1) add idemp table + unique index, 2) change reserve endpoint to upsert/return existing, 3) TTL + background reconciler to rollback/publish telemetry, 4) console dashboard: new graph for "reserve reuse rate" and an alert when reuse > 1% over 5m.

ana: agree. Also add a safeguard: when commit arrives, do a single atomic transition from pending->committed and reject double commit attempts (idempotent commit). If commit sees already committed -> return 200 with note. If commit sees pending expired -> return 410 and trigger reconciliation.

sasha: corner case: cross-region routing. If API servers in two regions try to create the idemp row concurrently, Postgres uniqueness at single region won't help unless we centralise the idemp store or shard by org with sticky routing. We need to either: 1) central idemp DB (global), 2) use strongly consistent kv (etcd/consul) for locks, or 3) route requests by org to a single canonical region.

lee: central DB seems simplest short term but we need performance tests. We'll batch benchmark ~2000 QPS reserve path. quota-bot: run canary TTL of 2s for contested keys.

mike: action items: 
- mike: write RFC with design + perf targets (due EOD Fri)
- sasha: prototype idemp table + upsert flow in staging (demo next Tue)
- ana: add tracing spans to link request_id -> reserve_id + emit metric reserve_reuse{org}
- lee: perf test plan and cross-region implications doc

ana: +1. Also add a short migration plan for older clients and a console note so support can explain behavior when idemp is reused.

mike: I'll own the dashboard alert. tagging @sasha @lee once RFC lands.

sasha: also put a small lint in SDKs to prefer exponential backoff and not retry on 202-with-reserve header; we'll coordinate with devex.

ana: thanks all. I'll attach the two sample traces to the thread for the postmortem.

billing-bot: FYI: created incident ticket #INC-2024-402 for duplicate-charge, linked to this thread.

mike: cool. ending thread — will follow up in RFC.
